question.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡2x=-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$ for $0\le x<\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}?$
question.worked_solution:
We will find the general solution to the equation, and then generate all of the solutions in the required domain.

The general solution to our equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi , & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi .\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the two equations above for $x$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}2x & =-\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi  & \, & \, & 2x & =\frac{5\pi }{6}+2n\pi  \\ x & =-\frac{5\pi }{12}+n\pi  & \, & \, & x & =\frac{5\pi }{12}+n\pi  \\ x & =\frac{(12n-5)\pi }{12} & \, & \, & x & =\frac{(12n+5)\pi }{12}\end{aligned}
$$

We set $n=0,\pm 1,\pm 2,…,$ until we have generated all solutions in the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

- Setting $n=0$ gives $x=-\frac{5\pi }{12}$ and $x=\frac{5\pi }{12}.$ We reject the solution $-\frac{5\pi }{12}$ since it lies outside the domain of interest.

- Setting $n=1$ gives $x=\frac{7\pi }{12}$ and $x=\frac{17\pi }{12}.$ We reject the solution $\frac{17\pi }{12}$ since it lies outside the domain of interest.

All other values of $n$ generate solutions outside the domain $0\le x<\pi .$

Finally,

$$
{x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}=\frac{5\pi }{12}\cdot \frac{7\pi }{12}=\frac{35{\pi }^{2}}{144}.
$$
